the method

six principles. every session, every door.

a word you already say, and the story underneath it
you don’t get a lecture. you get a word you already say — amen, namaste, salaam — and a session that hands it back with more in it. by the end it’s yours.
learn by doing
guess before you’re told. say it back into the mic. put the story in order. every session starts with you slightly wrong and ends with you right — the pattern the brain keeps.
native, and checked
your door, from your own texts, in your own words. a scholar of your tradition reads every session before a voice records it. nothing blended. nothing compared.
the hill, one breath at a time
day one is one breath. the sit grows over weeks, never in a jump. a streak that grows one lesson a day, with rest days built in, because every tradition knows rest. no guilt, no hearts.
a voice you already listen to
the reason a kid opens the app. licensed, with permission, reading only what a Keeper has checked. it never improvises.
a lantern for a friend
finish a day and light a lantern for someone. they get a link, walk a day, and can send one back. no feed, no followers.
what’s known

the evidence for practice is decades deep.

Harvard T.H. Chan · JAMA Internal Medicine, 2016
people who attended services more than weekly had about a third lower all-cause mortality over 16 years.
Li, VanderWeele et al. · 74,000+ women, Nurses’ Health Study
Harvard · JAMA Psychiatry, 2016
weekly attendance was associated with a roughly five-fold lower rate of suicide.
Li et al. · same cohort
Harvard · American Journal of Epidemiology, 2018
adolescents with a weekly practice were, years later, more likely to report high life satisfaction and to volunteer, and less likely to use drugs.
Chen & VanderWeele · 5,000+ youth
Pew Research Center, 2019
half of Catholics don’t know what their own church teaches about the Eucharist. religious literacy has fallen for decades.
What Americans Know About Religion

association isn’t causation, and none of these studies were about an app. they tell us the practice is worth making easy to start. whether this app does that is the question we’re paying to answer.

what we’re testing

our own studies, pre-registered, published whatever they say.

the pilot
a private beta, all eight doors. a handful of anonymous, opt-in events — never your answers.
the 100-day study
a pre-registered cohort measured with standard instruments — UCLA Loneliness Scale, PSS-10, WHO-5 — at day 1, 50 and 100, with an outside academic co-author who doesn’t work for us.
the literacy study, 2027
does a Camp 1 change what someone can explain about their own tradition? a before/after on Pew’s religious-knowledge questions, one door at a time.
the classroom study, 2027
a semester in a world-religions class: literacy, attitudes toward other traditions, and whether kids keep the practice after the grade is in.

for researchers

if you study religion, adolescence, loneliness or learning and want to work with the data or the cohort: a research address is coming soon. like every other address, it goes live the day the name does. every figure on this page goes through the research seat on the Keeper Desk and is re-checked against its source each year.

what we won’t claim

infinite hill is not therapy, medicine, or a substitute for a congregation, a clergy member or a doctor. it’s a daily practice. if you’re in a hard place, talk to a person — we’ll still be here.
